decisions.claim: B has been looking at or considering an apartment
decisions.reason: Turn 1 'What do you think about the apartment so far?' presupposes B has been looking at or considering the apartment; 'so far' implies ongoing evaluation.

decisions.claim: B is expected to move in to the apartment
decisions.reason: Turn 7 'before you move in' presupposes B will move into the apartment; this is a definite temporal presupposition.

decisions.claim: The apartment has a carpet with stains
decisions.reason: Turn 7 explicitly states 'Those stains will be cleaned out of the carpet,' confirming the apartment has a carpet with stains.

decisions.claim: B has mentioned at least one problem with the apartment
decisions.reason: Turn 9 'what other problems do you have?' uses 'other' which presupposes B has already mentioned at least one problem.

decisions.claim: B likes everything else about the apartment besides the problems mentioned
decisions.reason: Turn 11 'everything else is to your liking' is an explicit statement by A attributing a positive evaluation to B regarding aspects beyond the problems.

decisions.claim: B is considering moving into an apartment
decisions.reason: Same evidence as c2 but weaker: 'before you move in' presupposes B will move in (c2), not merely that B is 'considering' it (c6). c2 is the more complete and accurate claim.
decisions.counterexample: B might not be 'considering'—the presupposition is stronger: B is expected to move in.

decisions.claim: B has no problems with how the apartment looks
decisions.reason: Turn 3 'You don't have any problems with how it looks?' is a question seeking confirmation; it does not establish B's actual state. A is asking, not asserting.
decisions.counterexample: B could reply that they do have problems with how it looks.

decisions.claim: B mentioned stains on the carpet as a concern
decisions.reason: Cross-turn inference: Turn 5 'Like what?' asks B to specify problems, and Turn 7 responds about stains, implying B mentioned stains as a concern. Reasonable E2 presupposition from the dialogue flow.
decisions.counterexample: B might have mentioned a different problem and A pivoted to stains independently.

decisions.claim: B indicated everything else about the apartment is to their liking
decisions.reason: Same claim as c5 from the same evidence (Turn 11). c5 is the more precise formulation.

decisions.claim: B has been looking at or evaluating the apartment for some time
decisions.reason: Same evidence and essentially same claim as c1; 'so far' implies duration/ongoing evaluation which c1 already captures with 'looking at or considering.'
